canonical_question: How does the '10 nm change in grain size' specifically compare quantitatively to the thermal coarsening observed in the un-irradiated control sample at the same temperature?

question_variants.question: How does the '10 nm change in grain size' specifically compare quantitatively to the thermal coarsening observed in the un-irradiated control sample at the same temperature?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text reports a 10 nm grain size change during He implantation but does not provide data on the thermal coarsening of an un-irradiated control sample at the same temperature for direct quantitative comparison.

answers.answer: The text states that the material showed approximately 10 nm change in grain size during He implantation, but it does not provide the grain size evolution data for an un-irradiated control sample at the same temperature to allow for a quantitative comparison of thermal coarsening.
answers.measurement_outcome: Approximately 10 nm change in grain size
answers.boundary_limitation: No data on un-irradiated control thermal coarsening is available in the provided text.
evidence_spans: The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.
The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time

source_evidence_spans: Even though there was an increase in the grain size during He implantation, the material preserved its nano-crystallinity and showed only approximately 10 nm change in grain size
